title: Describing Clothes: size, colour, material
grammarTitle: Describing Clothes — size, colour, material, style
grammarNote:
Порядок прилагательных в английском — нельзя ставить в любом порядке!

📌 Официальный порядок (OSASCOMP):
Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose → NOUN

Пример: "a beautiful large old black French leather handbag"

На практике — 2-3 прилагательных подряд:
"a beautiful black dress" · "a lovely warm winter coat"
"a nice small silver ring" · "an old leather jacket"

💡 Самые частые комбинации:
Opinion + Colour: "a gorgeous red jacket"
Size + Colour: "a small blue backpack"
Age + Material: "an old leather bag"
Colour + Origin: "a black Italian suit"

⚠️ Типичные ошибки:
❌ "a leather old beautiful bag" → ✅ "a beautiful old leather bag"
❌ "a blue big warm coat" → ✅ "a big warm blue coat"

Запомни: мнение всегда первым, материал — последним перед существительным!

rows.example: where it sits on the body

pale pink / hot pink / dusty rose
I'm wearing a light blue cotton shirt.
She has a long dark red wool coat.
He's in a pair of slim-fit dark blue jeans.

He wore a traditional felt hat at the ceremony.
She prefers plain casual clothes for university.

grammarTip: Adjective order for clothes: Opinion → Size → Colour → Material → Noun. Example: "a beautiful (opinion) long (size) dark red (colour) wool (material) coat." Don't memorise all 8 categories — just know: opinion first, material last, colour before material.

exercises.instruction: Put adjectives in the correct order.
exercises.hint: Colour (light blue) before material (cotton): a light blue cotton shirt.

exercises.text: She wore a ___ (wool) coat to the ceremony.
exercises.hint: Material "wool" placed directly before the noun: a wool coat.

exercises.text: The opposite of "tight" in clothing is ___.
exercises.hint: "Loose" = not tight, with room to move. Tight ↔ loose.

exercises.text: "He wore a ___ checked shirt." Fill in with a size/fit word:
exercises.hint: "loose" describes fit (not tight). "striped" is a pattern, not a size word.

exercises.text: "Denim" is a type of material used for jeans.
exercises.hint: "Denim" = a strong cotton fabric used for jeans and jackets.

exercises.text: Kazakh traditional clothing uses ___ (a craft material made from pressed sheep wool).
exercises.hint: "Felt" = a material made by compressing wool fibres — used in Kazakh crafts.

opts: Deliberately larger than your normal size
exercises.correct: Deliberately larger than your normal size
exercises.hint: "Oversized" = intentionally larger than standard — a style choice.

exercises.text: Which is a pattern, not a colour?
exercises.hint: "Striped" = has stripes (a pattern). The others are colours.

exercises.text: She bought a second-___ leather jacket at the market.

opts: a beautiful long dark red wool coat
a wool long red dark beautiful coat
a dark red beautiful long wool coat
a long beautiful wool dark red coat
exercises.correct: a beautiful long dark red wool coat
exercises.hint: Opinion (beautiful) → size (long) → colour (dark red) → material (wool) → noun.

exercises.text: "Cotton" is breathable and suitable for everyday wear.
exercises.hint: "Cotton" = natural, breathable fabric — ideal for daily wear.

questions.hint: The general order is: opinion → size → colour → material → noun.

questions.text: She bought a beautiful ___ (size: not tight) dark red dress.
questions.hint: Size adjective comes after opinion: beautiful → long (size) → dark red (colour).

questions.text: "A wool beautiful coat" is in the correct order.
questions.hint: Correct: "a beautiful wool coat" — opinion (beautiful) before material (wool).
Loose = fitting loosely. Tight = fitting very close to the body.
"Silk" is a natural material. The others are pattern, style, and size.

questions.text: He wore a traditional Kazakh ___ hat at the ceremony.
questions.hint: "Felt" = a traditional material made from compressed wool, used in Kazakh crafts.

questions.text: "Charcoal, ash grey, light grey" are all:
questions.hint: These are all variations of the colour grey.
"Checked" is a pattern (a grid pattern). Others are material, material, and colour.

questions.text: She prefers wearing ___ casual clothes for university — jeans and a hoodie.
questions.hint: "Plain" = no pattern, one colour. Plain casual clothes = simple everyday wear.

questions.text: Why does Kamila say the jacket is too expensive?
opts: It costs more than her budget
questions.correct: It costs more than her budget
questions.hint: Statement 1: "She says the jacket is too expensive — it costs more than her budget."

questions.text: Kamila says the medium size is too big.
questions.hint: Statement 5: "She says the medium size is not big enough — she needs a large."

questions.text: What does Kamila ask at the end?
opts: If the jacket comes in a different colour
If there are any discounts available
If she can exchange it later
If it is on the website
questions.correct: If there are any discounts available
questions.hint: Statement 6: "She asks if the price is final or if there are any discounts available."
"Second-hand" = used by someone else before you.

questions.text: This cloth is too rough — I need a softer ___ for this dress.
questions.hint: "Material" or "fabric" = the type of cloth used to make clothing.

opts: Cheap clothes, high waste, low sustainability
questions.correct: Cheap clothes, high waste, low sustainability
questions.hint: "Fast fashion" = trend-driven cheap clothing that creates large amounts of waste.
